composition.serve_who: This sheet ('PORT/STBD CREW/GALLEY LTS', DWG GMMS 108'-119b, section captioned 'PORT AFT GUEST CABIN') is a Yachtica lighting-PLC wiring sheet. It documents three Yachtica controller modules (MCP 804 LX #8, MCP 804 LX #9, MGA BD4LX #21) that take switch-bank inputs (SW22, SW25, SW28, SW28.B, SW28.C) via terminal strip T/S D and output to numbered lighting circuits (8.1-8.4, 9.1-9.4, 21.1-21.4), plus a courtesy/emergency lighting tap and a shared CAN bus. All of the numbered CIRCUIT x.y loads and the COURTESY LIGHTS device are generic cabin lighting outputs of the Yachtica lighting-control system — the controllers, terminal strips, switch banks and CAN bus are the Yachtica system's own infrastructure (691-yachtica-lighting-control). The circuit labels do not name a specific cabin/space equipment node distinct from Yachtica itself (no separate 'crew' or 'galley' lighting circuit ids resolve individually beyond the sheet title), so the whole load bank is attributed to 691-yachtica-lighting-control as the serving system, with COURTESY LIGHTS additionally cross-referenced to 690-lts-courtesy since that circuit is its own established node.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Yachtica Lighting Control System (controllers #8, #9, #21 + switch banks + CAN bus)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The sheet is built entirely around three Yachtica controller modules (MCP 804 LX #8, MCP 804 LX #9, MGA BD4LX #21) which take switch-bank command inputs and drive numbered lighting output circuits via terminal strips. This matches the established Yachtica Lighting Control node (691-yachtica-lighting-control), previously fed via Q13/Q39 breakers on other sheets. The switch banks (SW22, SW25, SW28, SW28.B, SW28.C), T/S D terminal strip, and CAN bus are the system's own infrastructure/backbone, not separate equipment.

functions.label: Switch-bank command input to controller #8
functions.what_it_does: Nine-position switch banks SW22 and SW25 supply momentary/toggle command inputs into controller #8 (MCP 804 LX) via terminal strip T/S D terminals 1-9 (SW COM returns on terminals 10/11), giving the controller its lighting-scene/on-off commands for circuits 8.1-8.4.

flow_scenarios.path: SW22/SW25 switch contacts (open) -> T/S D terminals 1-9 -> controller #8 INPUTS 1-8, C -> no command asserted

SW22 or SW25 position n closed -> T/S D terminal n -> controller #8 INPUTS -> controller processes command -> drives output relay/driver stage for circuit 8.x -> SW COM return via T/S D terminals 10/11

functions.dry_data: MCP 804 LX controller #8, CAN-bus networked, +/- power feed via T/S D terminals 14/15, BUS A/B via terminals 12/13

functions.label: Switch-bank command input to controller #9
functions.what_it_does: Switch banks SW28, SW28.B, SW28.C supply command inputs into controller #9 (MCP 804 LX) via terminal strip T/S D terminals 17-24 (SW COM returns on 25/26/27), commanding lighting circuits 9.1-9.4 plus courtesy/emergency lighting taps.

flow_scenarios.path: SW28/SW28.B/SW28.C contacts open -> T/S D 17-24 -> controller #9 INPUTS -> no command asserted
SW28 family position closed -> T/S D terminal -> controller #9 INPUTS -> controller output stage energises corresponding circuit 9.x -> SW COM return via T/S D 25/26/27

functions.dry_data: MCP 804 LX controller #9, CAN-bus networked, +/- power feed via T/S D terminals 30/31, BUS A/B via terminals 28/29

functions.label: Controller #8 output to lighting circuits 8.1-8.4
functions.what_it_does: Controller #8 drives four independent lighting output circuits (8.1 16W, 8.2 4W, 8.3 24W, 8.4 16W) through fused output terminals 55-58; the shared +/+ supply pair at terminals 53/54 is itself protected by an inline 16A breaker before reaching the terminal bank.

flow_scenarios.path: controller #8 output stage open -> circuits 8.1-8.4 dark
controller #8 output block 1 -> fused terminal 55 -> CIRCUIT 8.1 (16W) lamp -> return to controller output common
controller #8 output block 2 -> fused terminal 56 -> CIRCUIT 8.2 (4W)
controller #8 output block 3 -> fused terminal 57 -> CIRCUIT 8.3 (24W)
controller #8 output block 4 -> fused terminal 58 -> CIRCUIT 8.4 (16W)

functions.dry_data: Loads: 16W/4W/24W/16W; supply pair fed via fused terminals 53/54 protected by 16A breaker

functions.label: Controller #9 output to lighting circuits 9.1-9.4
functions.what_it_does: Controller #9 drives four lighting output circuits (9.1 16W, 9.2 8W, 9.3 2W, 9.4 12W) through terminals 61-64; the shared supply pair at 59/60 is protected by an inline 16A breaker.

flow_scenarios.path: controller #9 output stage open -> circuits 9.1-9.4 dark
controller #9 output block 1 -> terminal 61 -> CIRCUIT 9.1 (16W)
controller #9 output block 2 -> terminal 62 -> CIRCUIT 9.2 (8W)
controller #9 output block 3 -> terminal 63 -> CIRCUIT 9.3 (2W)
controller #9 output block 4 -> terminal 64 -> CIRCUIT 9.4 (12W)

functions.dry_data: Loads: 16W/8W/2W/12W; supply pair fed via terminals 59/60 protected by 16A breaker

functions.label: Controller #21 (MGA BD4LX) 0-10V dimmer output to circuits 21.1-21.4
functions.what_it_does: Controller #21 (MGA BD4LX dimming module) drives four 0-10V dimmer DRIVER modules, each independently powering one dimmable lighting circuit (21.1-21.4, each 12W). Each DRIVER module's 230V AC L/N feed comes from the shared 230V AC supply block (L 230v / N / earth) via its own fused terminal (68 for driver 21.1's L, 69 for its N; 70/71 similarly feed the 21.2 driver's L/N pair per common-rail net16), while the 0-10V control signal comes from controller #21's output terminal block via terminals 44-48 (BUS A/B, +/-) and pin blocks 1-4.

flow_scenarios.path: controller #21 0-10V output at 0V -> DRIVER 0-10V module -> driver output dark/dimmed fully off -> CIRCUIT 21.x

230V AC L/N (net16, shared supply) -> fused terminal 68 (L) and 69 (N) -> DRIVER 0-10V (21.1) -> controller #21 0-10V command signal via terminal block 1-4 -> DRIVER output + / I -> CIRCUIT 21.1 (12W)
230V AC L/N (net16, shared supply) -> fused terminal 70 (L)/71 (N) region -> DRIVER 0-10V (21.2) -> controller #21 command -> CIRCUIT 21.2 (12W)
shared 230V AC supply (net16) -> DRIVER 0-10V (21.3)/(21.4) -> controller #21 0-10V command via 0V1-0V4 terminal strip -> CIRCUIT 21.3 (12W) / CIRCUIT 21.4 (12W)

functions.dry_data: 4x 12W dimmable circuits; drivers fed 230V AC via T/S 68/69 (and 70/71 for other drivers) off net16 common rail; 0-10V control bus 0V1-0V4

functions.label: System supply and shared CAN/bus infrastructure
functions.what_it_does: The whole Yachtica lighting-control node on this sheet is fed from AC 230V via breaker 'YACHTICA 10A' and, separately, +24V SERVICE BAT DC supply; PORT AFT GUEST CABIN LTS breaker Q43 (40A) supplies the associated cabin lighting loads. A CAN twisted-pair bus enters top-left and threads down through all three controllers (#8, #9, #21), providing their network/BUS A/B and command synchronisation, then exits bottom of sheet to continue elsewhere.

flow_scenarios.path: AC 230V supply -> breaker YACHTICA 10A -> feeds driver/DRIVER 230V rail (net16) and controller AC needs; +24V SERVICE BAT -> feeds controller DC power inputs (T/S D +/- terminals 14/15, 30/31, 46/47); CAN bus enters top-left -> routes through controllers #8/#9/#21 BUS A/B terminals -> exits bottom of sheet to continue off-sheet

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Courtesy Lights (courtesy/emergency lighting tap off Yachtica system)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: COURTESY LIGHTS is a distinct named load on this sheet fed via terminal 65 and controlled/tapped through the COURTESY/EMERGENCY LTS SW and EMERGENCY LTS SW terminals (66, 67). This matches the established courtesy-lighting node (690-lts-courtesy), which already has electrical_supply facts from other sheets (breaker Q37, etc.) — this sheet documents the local switch/terminal wiring for the courtesy lighting tap point within the Yachtica lighting infrastructure, not the courtesy circuit's own dedicated breaker (that lives on other sheets).

functions.label: Courtesy/emergency lighting switch loop
functions.what_it_does: A courtesy lighting output (terminal 65) is switched by a COURTESY/EMERGENCY LTS SW and a separate EMERGENCY LTS SW, both landing on terminals 66 and 67 respectively; walking the drawn lines, terminal 66 feeds/returns via the COURTESY/EMERGENCY LTS SW loop and terminal 67 via the EMERGENCY LTS SW loop, both associated with the COURTESY LIGHTS device.

flow_scenarios.path: COURTESY LIGHTS -> terminal 65 -> no switch closed -> lights off
terminal 66 -> COURTESY/EMERGENCY LTS SW closed -> COURTESY LIGHTS energised, return via terminal 66 junction
terminal 67 -> EMERGENCY LTS SW closed -> COURTESY LIGHTS energised (emergency override), return via terminal 67 junction

functions.dry_data: Courtesy lighting output on T/S D terminal 65; switch taps at terminals 66/67; local switch device identities (COURTESY/EMERGENCY LTS SW, EMERGENCY LTS SW) drawn only as arrows off-sheet — exact remote switch panel not shown here
